Fine Details Car Valeting Sprint Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Utmost Respect
runners_data.note: Prominent racer by style who won over 5f on Good last time out for Richard & Peter Fahey; strong sim-going record of 6 from 7 on similar surfaces, and the 3yo allowance could be a live edge here at OR 79 — 43 days off is manageable.|

runners_data.name: Kinnalargy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Kevin Ryan who has a perfect 9-from-9 record on sim-going, meaning Good turf is no issue; the danger is having his lead contested by Managing Director from the outset, which could see him burn brighter than his finishing kick allows.|

runners_data.name: Call To Action
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up performer whose last five runs show a pattern of second finishes on Good and this trip suits well; natural style is to come from deep, and with a clean run from Joanna Mason this course-proven speedster is the most credible late threat.|

runners_data.name: Sports Coach
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with honest recent form showing consecutive seconds, though all coming in behind good rivals; no Going concern but the sheer traffic in a 22-runner sprint makes his preferred last-to-first style a logistical challenge today.|

runners_data.name: Explosive Finnish
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo who won last time over 6f on Good and has finished placed at 5f and 6f on similar going repeatedly; sits naturally in a prominent role and should slot in comfortably behind the two leaders without fighting for position — the trip slightly sharper than his recent wins but his TS trend is rising.|

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Prominent veteran who won over 5f on Good and carries a visor; runs frequently (16 days back) for a trainer firing at 3 from 25 over the T14 window — well-travelled at this track and trip combination with the form to suggest he can place even if not win outright.|

runners_data.name: True Promise
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose Good-going record is thin (4 from 15 sim-going) and only one placed finish on similar surface in last five; returning in 17 days but trainer T14 is 0 from 2, and the form string shows inconsistency over the trip.|

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer who has placed four times in last five outings on sim-going; finishing third twice recently on Good at 6f but steps down to 5½f — the extra pace at this distance may suit him arriving late if traffic allows.|

runners_data.name: Little Mi Mi
runners_data.note: Two wins in last five on sim-going for Iain Jardine and sits naturally in the prominent group; form figures of 113 in recent starts signal live form and the step back to 5f on Good turf plays to the preference shown in her last winning effort.|

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: Strong Going-course profile with 11 from 15 sim-going records and two wins in the last five; natural hold-up type with Jason Hart up — if anyone can thread a route through 22 runners late, this mare's course-familiarity and Good-ground relish makes her the most reliable of the closers.|

runners_data.name: Duran
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing hold-up type who has been out of form recently with a string of 11th-16th finishes; 17 days since last run for Nigel Tinkler who is 0 from 22 over the T14 window, and nothing in the recent profile encourages confidence despite Good-ground ability in theory.|

runners_data.name: Vingegaard
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a visor who did win over 6f on Good earlier in the season but has posted 14th and 12th in his last two; 39 days off and a tricky assignment in a field this size from a deep position.|

runners_data.name: Copper Knight
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent racer aged 12 who carries a tongue-tie and has been busy recently (17 days); OR 74 and recent form figures include a 1 over course and distance but has also thrown in several double-digit finishes — at peak age but experience counts in big fields.|

runners_data.name: Managing Director
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a sim-going record of 8 from 9 and a recent course-distance win over 5f on Good; P J McDonald is a smart booking for a horse who wants to get on with it, and if he avoids a flat-out war with Kinnalargy he has real place prospects.|

runners_data.name: Roach Power
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator by nature — his real home is at the back of the field — but with so many closers in this field he is mapped mid-division, meaning he may find himself racing forward of his comfort zone; form on firm/Good is only modest (7 from 15 sim-going) and the 8-day turnaround is short.|

runners_data.name: Kanishka
runners_data.note: Dropping sharply in trip from 8f to 5½f for Ian Williams; prominent style but class may not translate as readily as it sounds — recent form shows 11th at 5f on Good and a consistent pattern of failing to fire at shorter distances, though OR 72 gives weight room.|

runners_data.name: Bonnie's Boy
runners_data.note: By instinct a horse who wants the back of the field, but the congestion of hold-up types means he is likely to end up racing mid-division rather than in his preferred position — his Good-going form (7 from 15 sim-going) is solid but he needs the right run in a packed field.|

runners_data.name: Ventura Express
runners_data.note: Prolific hold-up performer aged nine who consistently finishes 4th to 6th on Good and soft; his true trailing style is compromised today given how many closers are competing for the same rear-of-field real estate — honest but limited upside at this stage of his career.|

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type whose recent form shows a second and a fourth on Good at 5f, so the going and trip work; among the redistributed closers he has arguably the most recent competitive form, but Paul Mulrennan will need to work hard to find daylight through a 22-runner field from a position that is already further forward than ideal.|

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Has won twice in last five outings (including on Going and Heavy) and is only 3 days off a run — very fresh returns can be sharp for this type; hold-up natural but trainer Tristan Davidson has a strong T14 strike rate of 5 from 11, and the recent winning form at 5f deserves respect even from a compromised positional draw.|

runners_data.name: Maharajas Express
runners_data.note: Two wins from 10 on sim-going and a recent second at 5f on Good showing the form is live; by nature a hold-up runner, so racing further forward than preferred means David Egan will need to manage him carefully — the OR 68 gives him a weight edge that could matter.|

runners_data.name: Tanjen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Tim Easterby's powerful stable (T14: 12 from 80) who won over 5f on Good earlier in the season; at OR 66 he carries the lightest weight in the field, which is a meaningful factor in a competitive handicap, and his recent third on soft suggests the form is ticking over.|

races.paceDynamic: Kinnalargy and Managing Director are the two confirmed front-runners in a 22-runner field, and with both likely to push forward from the off, this 5½f York sprint will be run at an honest, pressured gallop from the first stride rather than building gradually. That sustained early tempo on Good turf over a straight course will stretch the field quickly, creating a race where positional advantage close to the pace is premium real estate — prominent racers who can slot in just behind the leaders without burning fuel fighting for position will be optimally placed. The sheer size of the field means hold-up horses face a genuine challenge: Roach Power, Bonnie's Boy, Ventura Express, Oriental Prince, Harb, and Maharajas Express are all true hold-up types that the map has redistributed into midfield because there is simply not enough rear-of-field space for all of them — Roach Power and Ventura Express are most likely to actually secure a trailing position, while others will find themselves racing closer than natural. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours horses with a prominent style who can track the contested pace and produce a finish from a handy position, rather than those forced to come from deep in a big, fast-moving field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Kinnalargy and Managing Director set a true contested gallop and the race resolves in favour of horses sitting just off them.
scenarios.body: The pressured pace from the two leaders sets up perfectly for the prominent stalkers — horses like Explosive Finnish, Little Mi Mi, and Utmost Respect can track the speed without fighting for it and produce their finish at the two-furlong marker. On Good turf at York over this straight 5½f, the horse with the cleanest passage from a handy position wins, and this profile is best served by the race shape on offer.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Sustain
scenarios.trigger: If Kinnalargy or Managing Director dictates from the front without being seriously challenged and finds enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: One of the two leaders gets a fraction of daylight from a poor break by the other, effectively converting a contested into a semi-controlled gallop from their own position, and their natural pace-preference becomes an asset rather than a liability. Managing Director's strong Good-ground sim-going record and recent course form gives this shape real teeth — a front-runner winning a big-field sprint by simply not being caught is a well-trodden York outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is exceptionally fierce and burns through the prominent horses, creating late ground for horses from further back.
scenarios.body: Call To Action and Curious Rover both carry strong form at this trip on Good and have the profile to motor late if the pace is truly suicidal, though in a field this large getting a clear run is the key variable. The redistribution caveat applies: several horses mapped mid-field are not genuine hold-up types, so the true closers who can capitalise are fewer than the field size suggests — Call To Action and Curious Rover are the most credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners burn each other out quickly and a midfield horse with tactical speed picks up the pieces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This shape requires the pace to be so extreme that it unravels entirely, allowing a horse like Tanjen or Kanishka to motor through from mid-division as the leaders tie up — a lower-probability outcome given Good ground that shouldn't accelerate deterioration unusually. Kanishka drops sharply in trip here having run over a mile but carries class form, and Tanjen showed a winning turn of foot on Good at this trip recently for a powerful stable.

watchPoints.text: Kinnalargy and Managing Director are on a collision course for the early lead — watch the first furlong for which of the two gets their nose in front first, as the one that has to fight hardest for position may fade before the straight narrows.|

Little Mi Mi has won twice in recent outings and sits naturally in a prominent role for a stable that is 3 from 25 over the T14 window — if she gets a clean passage tracking the pace she becomes a serious winning threat that may be underestimated.|

The redistribution of Roach Power, Bonnie's Boy, Ventura Express, Oriental Prince, Harb, and Maharajas Express into midfield creates a dangerous pocket of horses racing out of role — watch for interference and traffic issues in the final two furlongs as these horses seek gaps that may not exist.|

Harb returns just 3 days after a run and is trained by Tristan Davidson who is striking at 5 from 11 over the T14 window — very short-turnaround runners for in-form yards in big handicap sprints can catch the market cold.|

races.name: Hanson Springs Stayers Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Shadow Dance
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner with Rebecca Menzies saddling; her recent form is poor (7-6700) and all five history runs came on softer-than-Good ground, so the Good surface is a live concern at this extreme trip — her style-fit tag reflects that she is unlikely to reproduce her best here even if she controls the pace.

runners_data.name: Pinatique
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's hold-up filly has a 6/19 14-day strike rate which is notable; her history runs max out at 12f on Good or Heavier ground and she has zero wins or places in six sim-going starts, making this step up to 2m½f on Good a significant ask without solid evidence it suits.

runners_data.name: Percy Shelley
runners_data.note: Prominent type with an outstanding sim-going record of 2W10P from 14 runs on Good, all over 14f-20f; the James Owen yard is 2/36 in 14 days so no red-hot form, but this horse clearly handles York-type galloping tracks and the Good surface exceptionally well and has every right to run a big race.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: Has won four of 14 runs on Good ground and recorded back-to-back 16f wins on Good, making this the ideal surface and trip combination; prominent style suits a steady pace scenario perfectly, the visor adds focus, and James Owen running two horses from the same yard creates interesting tactical options.

runners_data.name: Call My Bluff
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Good and is a proven hold-up performer; the 91-day absence is the headline concern, and his history shows wide spread of form from 1st to 17th, but he wears a hood for headgear and the Good ground is in his comfort zone over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Rock N Roll Pinkie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose five history runs are all on Good or Firm-adjacent and shows 2W4P from nine sim-going starts; Silvestre De Sousa is a strong booking in a handicap, but the horse has not finished better than fourth in recent starts and the 16f-20f distance band suits without him being dominant.

runners_data.name: Moon Chime
runners_data.note: Has two wins on Good ground at 16f and Callum Hutchinson takes over; the 50-day absence needs monitoring but his profile — proven on Good, suited by long trips, genuine hold-up style — fits a scenario where the pace is honest enough to allow a late run from a settled position.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Prominent type who handles Good well (2W5P from 10 sim-going runs) and Jim Goldie is in form at 3/29 in 14 days; ran three days ago over a shorter trip, so freshness is worth monitoring, but Paul Mulrennan is a reliable booking and Trojan Sun's consistency at 16f-18f on Good makes him a solid prominent tracker.

runners_data.name: Florida Dreams
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse by nature — has barely run at 2m+ and all history runs are on softer ground; pushed into a midfield mapping because of the surplus of closers, but her true closing style is constrained here, her sim-going record is sparse (0W1P from 2 runs), and the step up in trip from 9f-12f-territory form is steep.

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up type who has placed at 14f on Good but whose natural closing style will be compromised by being mapped closer to the pace than ideal; three of five history runs at 14f on Good produced only one placing, and the 0W1P sim-going record offers limited encouragement at this extra distance.

runners_data.name: Marbuzet
runners_data.note: Has won on Heavier ground and has seven places from 12 sim-going runs but only at up to 16f; the 7-day turnaround is very quick, Jake Dickson claims 5lb which helps, and his natural hold-up tendencies will be diluted by the redistribution — a horse capable of running well but needing everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Prominent type with two wins on Good at 14f-16f and a strong sim-going record of 2W5P; Jack Nicholls claims 3lb and the Iain Jardine yard is 3/25 in 14 days — a horse who has form at big tracks on Good and whose light weight combination makes him a legitimate player if he secures his natural position off the pace.

runners_data.name: Furhaan
runners_data.note: Young Jim Goldie-trained hold-up type who is 11/12 on Good ground historically but has no wins; Lauren Young claims 5lb which alleviates the top of the handicap concern, and recent finishes of 4-3-2 at 16f-18f on Good suggest improving profile — though his true hold-up style, pushed forward by redistribution, may not allow him to finish as powerfully as his recent form implies.

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Dance is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with a genuinely sustainable pace expected over this 2m½f trip at York on Good ground, she is likely to dictate from the front without serious pressure. Percy Shelley, High Fibre, Trojan Sun, and Newport are the prominent types who will look to track her closely, creating a compact, organised early order rather than a scrappy scramble for position. The field contains more true hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Florida Dreams, Gibside, Marbuzet, and Furhaan are genuine closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would naturally like, diluting their finishing kick. At 2m½f on a flat, galloping track with a steady, uncontested fractions scenario, prominent racers who can travel fluently just off Shadow Dance and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Dance sets an uncontested, even tempo and the prominent holders track her comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: High Fibre and Percy Shelley, both proven at this trip on Good ground with strong records at 14f+, travel within striking distance and have the stamina and recent form to overhaul Shadow Dance from two furlongs out. Trojan Sun and Newport, also prominent types, are secondary beneficiaries of this even gallop that rewards those who travel efficiently rather than finishing from far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong early and the field strings out, giving genuine hold-up horses room to finish.
scenarios.body: Moon Chime, who has won twice on Good over 16f and handles a galloping track, would be the most natural beneficiary with a well-timed late run; Call My Bluff, a course winner and proven hold-up performer on Good, could also pick up the pieces if the pace fractions are honest enough to create a finishing opportunity. The redistributed hold-up types — Gibside, Marbuzet, Furhaan — are less well-placed to deliver this scenario given they will not be at the back of the field where their acceleration is best deployed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Dance produces a true front-runner's display, dictating a searching gallop that grinds out all rivals.
scenarios.body: Shadow Dance has tactical pace and is not being pressed, but her recent form string of 7-6700 and OR of 86 over an extreme trip on softer surfaces is a genuine concern; if she can replicate her best prominent-style performance this is a live scenario, though her style-fit tag tempers confidence. Percy Shelley, who has two wins at 16f+ on Good and excellent sim-going figures, would be the horse most likely to match her toe-to-toe if the pace is grinding rather than electric.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group fails to settle and fragments the pace, causing a rough race shape where none of the tactical strategies fully unfolds.
scenarios.body: With multiple prominent types — Percy Shelley, High Fibre, Trojan Sun, Newport — all seeking the same position behind Shadow Dance, interference or pace spikes could disrupt rhythm and randomise the result. Newport, who has won twice over similar trips on Good and carries a light weight with an apprentice claiming 3lb, would be among those most likely to benefit from any positional chaos in a race with scrambled running positions.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Dance's ability to control the early tempo without being pressured is the pivotal factor — if Percy Shelley or Trojan Sun push her pace even slightly, the fractions could unravel the whole field shape from the front.

High Fibre and Percy Shelley are trained by the same yard (James Owen) — watch for any tactical understanding between them in the prominent group, as one could effectively set things up for the other over the final two furlongs.

Florida Dreams, Gibside, Marbuzet, and Furhaan are all natural closers who cannot race from their preferred deep position in this field — any one of them trapped wide or forced to race keenly from a non-natural spot could run well below their best and distort closing-run expectations.

Moon Chime's 50-day absence is worth tracking in the market and in the paddock; she has two wins at 16f on Good and is a proven hold-up horse, but returning off a break at 2m½f demands she is fit enough to finish her race properly.

Newport's apprentice claim of 3lb from Jack Nicholls is notable in a competitive handicap — the weight advantage over prominent rivals who carry more could prove decisive if the pace is even and positions are settled by halfway.

races.name: Saltmoore Collection Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Noble Horizon
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good going over this sort of trip and has course form; a genuine hold-up performer for De Sousa who will need a clear run late in a compressed field, but sim-going record (10/12) is encouraging.|

runners_data.name: Nesthorn
runners_data.note: George Baker's four-year-old has placed twice in his last five and prefers to come from well off the pace, which is his natural rhythm; a wide draw or midfield scrimmage could limit him but he handles Good ground and the longer trip suits.|

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: David Egan's mount has a prominent style that makes him one of the most naturally placed runners behind Double Parked; Tinkler's 0/22 14-day record is poor but this horse's Good-ground form is solid and the trip is within range.|

runners_data.name: Teumessias Fox
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding sends this seven-year-old back from softer ground and a P (pulled up) recently clouds confidence; sim-going record on Good is weak (5/15, no wins) and McDonald will need a trouble-free passage from hold-up.|

runners_data.name: Have Secret
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr partners this Fahey six-year-old who wears a visor and has been disappointing lately (three consecutive zeros), though his one career win on Good at 10f offers some hope; needs traffic to part promptly.|

runners_data.name: Let's Dream
runners_data.note: Three wins in recent Good-ground form over this sort of trip make him statistically interesting; Hector Crouch drops into a big-field handicap and the horse's natural hold-up style means he requires a gap to appear at the right moment.|

runners_data.name: Duke's Command
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's five-year-old returns from 115 days off, which is a significant freshness query; a natural hold-up type pressed into midfield in this shape, the style-fit discount (0.92) and lengthy absence make this a speculative each-way at best.|

runners_data.name: Castle Stuart
runners_data.note: Fahey's four-year-old wears a hood and carries recent Good-ground placed form (2nd, 3rd) at this trip; his natural closing style is squeezed into midfield by the field's density, tempering how much his form entitles him to.|

runners_data.name: Besieged
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's unexposed three-year-old ran 1-2-2 in his three starts and steps up from 10f on softer ground; Lewis Edmunds takes the ride and the prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Double Parked — the key unknown is whether the OR-93 mark is fair after limited runs.|

runners_data.name: Dark Moon Rising
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's seven-year-old won over this trip on Good at 10f last time but the redistribution into midfield means Tom Eaves must navigate 16 rivals; headgear (p, first-time blinkers) could sharpen focus but also risk burning energy early.|

runners_data.name: Dhahabi
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's eight-year-old has a bleak recent record (00-000) and the headgear note (t, tongue-tie) has done little to reverse that; a true hold-up type forced into a compressed midfield, the form and style-fit discount combine to make this a very low-probability runner.|

runners_data.name: Empire Of Light
runners_data.note: Won three of his last six and carries a prominent style that naturally puts him in the box seat on a track where Grant Tuer won with him recently; 85 days off is a query but the Going is right and the form peak at 10f matches today's distance.|

runners_data.name: Wahdan
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old ran only seven days ago and races with headgear (p); a true hold-up performer shifted into midfield on the map, the quick turnaround and apprentice Jake Dickson (5lb claim) make for a complex profile, though recent 3rds and 4ths show consistent effort.|

runners_data.name: Double Parked
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner for Easterby and David Allan; won over this course and distance on Good and sets his own fractions here without challenge — the critical variable is whether his low OR (83) is exposed by better-handicapped rivals once they close in the final furlong.|

runners_data.name: Wanderlust
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's four-year-old wears blinkers (b) and has placed four times in his last five runs at 10-12f; a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield, Andrew Mullen must find room in a big, compacted field — the blinkers may help him hold a position more assertively.|

runners_data.name: Pearl River
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old has a prominent style and won at 10f on Good; Alec Voikhansky takes the mount and the yard's 14-day strike rate (1/52) is poor, but the horse's natural position close to Double Parked is a tactical asset in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Donny
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has been placed four times in five but has yet to win; 58 days off and a natural hold-up style redistributed into midfield means Duran Fentiman will need significant fortune in running in a 17-runner handicap — consistent but short of the required class jump.|

races.paceDynamic: Double Parked is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, David Allan can dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 1m2½f at York. The prominent horses — Tuscan Hills, Besieged, Empire Of Light and Pearl River — will look to track him in the early positions, but the tempo Double Parked sets is unlikely to be pressured, meaning the pace will be genuine without being genuinely hot. This race shape — a steady-to-fair pace with a single leader and a cluster of prominent types behind — classically favours horses who can race prominently and quicken through the final two furlongs rather than those forced to make up ground from the rear of a big field. The field holds materially more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the back: Duke's Command, Castle Stuart, Dhahabi, Dark Moon Rising, Wahdan, Wanderlust and Stoneacre Donny are all genuine closers who will be compressed into midfield, meaning true late-running room will be fiercely contested and those redistributed horses face a compromised scenario; Nesthorn and Noble Horizon are best-placed among the authentic hold-up runners to find clear daylight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Double Parked sets a controlled, uncontested gallop and the finish revolves around those who tracked him from two to four lengths off the pace.
scenarios.body: Double Parked rolls along in front with Tuscan Hills, Besieged and Empire Of Light close up, and when the pace quickens in the final quarter-mile the horses who saved ground and energy mid-race have first run on the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Double Parked's front-running is so well-judged that he sets a tempo just slow enough to preserve his stamina and kicks clear before closers can organise.
scenarios.body: With 17 runners compressing the midfield and the hold-up horses unable to find a clean passage, Double Parked's unchallenged lead gives him a first-run advantage that proves decisive as the closers are stymied in traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find A Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected or Double Parked weakens sharply, allowing hold-up horses who navigate traffic cleanly to swoop late.
scenarios.body: Noble Horizon and Nesthorn — the truest hold-up types who avoid the redistribution congestion — would be best placed to weave through in the final furlong if there is a wall of beaten horses to run past.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Scrambles
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so pedestrian that it causes a bunched finish and a sprint for home catches everyone flat-footed.
scenarios.body: Let's Dream has won off similar marks on Good ground and possesses the cruising speed to produce a sharp turn of foot in a race that becomes a sprint; Pearl River's prominent style positions her to react quickly.

watchPoints.text: Double Parked (front-runner, David Allan) — watch whether he is allowed a completely uncontested lead; if any prominent horse harasses him in the first half-mile, the whole tempo calculation changes and closing styles gain significantly.

Besieged — the three-year-old has run only three times and steps sharply up in class and field size; if Lewis Edmunds misjudges the pace in the early stages, the unexposed form could be exposed or, conversely, a clean prominent run could make him dangerously well-in.

Noble Horizon and Nesthorn — both are genuine hold-up horses in a field where seven redistributed closers are all seeking the same late ground; watch the draw and early positioning, as a blocked passage for either in the straight could be decisive.

Empire Of Light — returns from 85 days off with three wins in his recent profile; if Grant Tuer has him tuned for this first run back, the prominent style is ideally placed, but watch for any signs of race-rustiness in the first few furlongs.

Dark Moon Rising (headgear: first-time blinkers noted as p) — new headgear on a seven-year-old in a 17-runner handicap can produce an unpredictable early reaction; if the blinkers cause him to race more freely than usual, Tom Eaves may find him fighting the hold-up brief entirely.

races.name: Starman At Tally Ho Stud Garrowby Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Behike
runners_data.note: Won twice over 6f on good ground recently and arrives in good form, but his natural prominent style cannot be accommodated at the head of a field already packed with front-rank types — he will find himself racing further back than ideal, which places a real question mark over his ability to reproduce those wins from a compromised position.

runners_data.name: Dickensian
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse trained by Kevin Ryan, whose yard is 4/33 in the past fortnight, with a solid course record of 10 runs on good going producing two wins and six placings — he is the most authentic closer in the race and has the cleanest profile for a scenario where the pace collapses or the front rank is congested.

runners_data.name: Double Rush
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who has won three of his last four over six furlongs on good ground and carries the key tactical role of setting the tempo — 57 days off the track is a mild flag, but Andrew Balding's operation travels runners confidently and his style-fit to the race shape is the highest of any runner here.

runners_data.name: Regional
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran with exceptional course familiarity (14 runs on good ground at this trip-class combination, three wins and nine places), trained by Edward Bethell who is 3/22 in the past fortnight — he knows how to travel prominently and deliver at York, though a string of modest recent finishes suggests he needs things to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Spycatcher
runners_data.note: The highest-rated horse in the field at OR 111 and a genuine hold-up runner for K.R. Burke, but 106 days off the track is a significant concern and his five good-ground runs at 6f have produced zero wins or places — the layoff means he needs to hit the ground running in what is a hot Listed race.

runners_data.name: Extremely Zain
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old from William Haggas carrying a 3lb sex allowance, with two wins over seven furlongs on good ground before making a winning debut at six furlongs — drops in trip brings freshness, and Cieren Fallon's low-key booking for a Haggas string that is 9/48 in the past fortnight gives him tactical options near the front.

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly dropping back to a distance she won over on good ground (1/6f/GOO in latest), trained by Richard Hughes who is 4/28 in the past fortnight — Daniel Tudhope's course knowledge and her ability to race prominently make her one of the prime beneficiaries of the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: Nariko
runners_data.note: A five-year-old returning after 302 days off the track, which alone makes her a significant risk in a Listed race; she has winning form over 6f on good ground but her true prominent racing style cannot be accommodated in this front-heavy field, and the combination of long absence and positional difficulty makes her very hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Lam Yai
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's second string (alongside Spycatcher), a three-year-old who has been racing prominently in her last five runs — she will want to be up with the pace but this field is already full in that space, and her recent form at six furlongs on good ground (3rd and 4th) does not suggest she has the class to win a Listed race from a suboptimal position.

races.paceDynamic: Double Rush is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the gate, he will control tempo from the off at a measured, sustainable gallop on good ground over six furlongs at York. Extremely Zain, America Queen, and Regional will all push for prominent positions just behind him, creating a compressed, bunched shape through the first two furlongs rather than a true speed duel. This field carries a significant surplus of prominent-style horses — Behike, Lam Yai, and Nariko are all natural up-with-pace types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because Double Rush, Extremely Zain, America Queen, and Regional will fill the front rank first; of those, Extremely Zain and America Queen are most likely to actually secure prominent ground given their class and recent form. With a single front-runner setting an honest but unforced pace and a wall of prominent types sitting just behind, the race favours horses who can race on or near the pace from the outset and sustain their effort into the final furlong — pure hold-up finishers face a congested route through and will need significant gaps to open late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Double Rush Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Double Rush sets a sustainable solo gallop and the prominent horses directly behind him fire off his pace turning for home.
scenarios.body: Double Rush dictates throughout at a gallop that suits his competitors sitting within two lengths of him, and when the sprint for home begins the horses in the front rank have first run with no traffic issues. Extremely Zain and America Queen, both proven on good ground over this course and distance, are ideally placed to pounce if Double Rush ties up in the final strides.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Double Rush sets a falsely fast early tempo and ties up inside the final two furlongs, allowing hold-up horses to deliver from the rear.
scenarios.body: A pace collapse would open a gap for Dickensian and Spycatcher, both genuine hold-up types who will be tracking the field and conserving energy through the early stages. Dickensian has strong course form over five furlongs on good ground and the extra furlong at York may help him sustain his late run, while Spycatcher's long absence makes this scenario less reliable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent-style horses ignites a pace battle in the first two furlongs as Behike, Lam Yai, or Nariko push to reclaim their natural positions.
scenarios.body: Should the crowded front rank create genuine early pressure, the pace could burn off the principals and leave the race open for hold-up horses arriving late with a strong wind at their backs. Dickensian is the primary beneficiary of this shape given his pattern of finishing from the rear on cut-free ground, though the scenario depends on redistrubuted horses disrupting the pace enough to matter.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tight Photo Finish, Midfield Shuffle
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is perfectly even and every horse lands in a congested finish over the last furlong.
scenarios.body: A uniform tempo with no clear winner from the prominent rank creates a blanket finish where positional luck and a decisive jockey ride prove decisive. Regional's veteran course craft and Behike's finishing speed, if he manages to find clear running despite his displaced position, could bring them into the picture.

watchPoints.text: Double Rush's early tempo is the race's defining variable — if Shane Foley allows him to coast in front unchallenged the prominent horses directly behind him will travel sweetly, but any sign of interference from the redistributed prominent types in the first furlong could change the entire complexion of the race.

Spycatcher's 106-day absence is the longest layoff in the field for a horse entering at Listed level — watch whether he moves fluently in the preliminaries and travels smoothly early, as K.R. Burke runners returning from big breaks can be ring-rusty before finding their best.

Behike, Lam Yai, and Nariko are all genuine prominent racers squeezed out of their natural ground — watch the opening two furlongs for any scrimmaging as these three try to recover position, since even a small pace flare-up here would significantly alter the race shape and redistribute benefit toward the hold-up horses.

Nariko's 302-day layoff is extreme even by comeback standards — watch her in the parade ring and early strides to assess whether Hugo Palmer has her ready to perform at this level first time out after such a long break.

The three-year-old fillies (Extremely Zain and America Queen) both carry sex allowances and are lightly-raced relative to their older rivals — if either travels with unusual ease in behind Double Rush through the first four furlongs, they may have more in the tank than their ratings suggest when the race ignites.

races.name: Eboracum Security Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: He's A Monster
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse off a long 378-day absence, which is a significant query; five similar-going runs return modest form, and from this position he needs a perfect passage that a 15-runner field may not provide.

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old front-of-midfield type who is rock-solid on Good ground (14 of 15 runs), won over 7f at York before, and Connor Beasley knows the course well — strong each-way profile.

runners_data.name: Bobby Bennu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian runner wearing headgear (h), keen prominent style suits the trip, but a form line of 50-420 lacks a winning punch and he is 39 days since a run; Good ground suits him.

runners_data.name: Power Fizz
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner; William Haggas horses are firing at nearly 19% in 14 days, Fallon can dictate from the front, and two of his last five on Good have been wins — the structural key to this race.

runners_data.name: Houquetot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form (65-974) is patchy; four of five runs on Good ground produced just one placing, and 64 days since last run adds further caution on fitness grounds.

runners_data.name: Great Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent type running for a trainer who has drawn a blank in six recent runners; won at 8f on Soft but York's 7f on Good is a different test — no wins in three attempts at this track configuration.

runners_data.name: Khafiz
runners_data.note: Off 22 days, four-year-old hold-up horse whose Good-ground record at 7f shows a placed effort but also wide-margin defeats; form string 500440 does not inspire, yet the trip and going are fine.

runners_data.name: Utmost Good Faith
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type, 21 days fresh, wearing headgear (ht) for Stuart Williams; two Good-ground wins in form, but a 12-13 in his last two at 7f on Good suggests inconsistency — Kaiya Fraser takes a 3lb claim.

runners_data.name: Humam
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' other runner, a genuine hold-up specialist by nature but redistributed into the midfield on the map due to the density of hold-up types; 11 similar-going runs place the burden of proof firmly on finding a clean run.

runners_data.name: Mr Noble
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old is lightly raced and in fine nick — four of five runs a place, trained at a 10/39 clip in 14 days; 7f on Good is unexplored upside territory and he races off a low weight.

runners_data.name: Our Havana
runners_data.note: Genuine closer by trade, having won over 7f at York before — the course form is there — but the redistribution into a midfield map position reflects that too many horses are chasing the same real estate at the back; 36 days since running.

runners_data.name: U Sure Do
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby 12/80 in 14 days, seven-year-old prominent type, 15 days fresh and wears a tongue-tie; three wins from 15 on similar going, trips and form suggest solid rather than brilliant.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Fascinating form string of 222222 — highly consistent but seemingly incapable of winning; a natural closer whose true positioning is compromised by redistribution, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim must be weighed against whether the horse can ever get her head in front.

runners_data.name: First Time
runners_data.note: Fahey runner, 36 days fresh, three of last four runs placed on Good ground at 7f — reliable each-way profile; not obviously the yard's first string with Our Havana also running.

runners_data.name: Quest For Fun
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old natural prominent racer who cannot reclaim that position in this congested field; mapped to midfield against her inclinations with a STYLE_FIT warning, and recent form 955303 reflects a horse just off the pace enough to frustrate.

races.paceDynamic: Power Fizz is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to match strides from the outset, Cieren Fallon can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good ground at York. The prominent pack — Northern Express, Bobby Bennu, Great Dream, Mr Noble, U Sure Do, and First Time — is congested, with six runners all seeking the same territory two to three furlongs out, creating a real risk of traffic trouble and interference through the mid-race. Quest For Fun is a natural prominent type who cannot realistically win the position battle in this field and has been mapped to midfield against her grain, while Humam, Our Havana, and Woohoo are true hold-up horses shuffled into the midfield picture purely by redistribution — their effectiveness as late closers is compromised by that overcrowding. The race shape strongly favours a front-running or close-prominent profile: with Power Fizz setting a measured pace and a congested chasing pack likely running into each other, the tactical verdict is clear — horses racing prominently behind the leader, or indeed Power Fizz herself, hold the structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Power Fizz Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Power Fizz is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and the prominent pack burns each other out competing for second position.
scenarios.body: Power Fizz dictates a fair but manageable gallop on Good ground, and the congestion behind means no single rival can organise a clean, coordinated challenge; Fallon times the injection of pace to deny closers getting into range.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stretch Power Fizz, allowing a prominent-ridden horse to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting second or third on the heels of Power Fizz avoids the worst of the mid-race scrimmaging and pounces as the leader's effort flattens out in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Benefits Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent bunch cause serious interference two furlongs out, opening a gap for a horse travelling sweetly through the centre of the field.
scenarios.body: A midfield runner who finds a clean passage as the prominent wall implodes can pick up ground rapidly through the final furlong on this fair, flat York track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Power Fizz sets an unexpectedly strong pace that brings the field back to the redistributed hold-up types in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This shape requires Humam, Our Havana, or Woohoo to find clear daylight having been forced to race against their natural instincts closer to the pace; the structural deficit makes this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Power Fizz (Cieren Fallon) is the only horse capable of making all — watch whether any of the six prominent runners attempt to press from the first furlong, as any early pressure could radically alter the pace shape and compromise the most likely scenario.

The prominent cluster of Northern Express, Bobby Bennu, Great Dream, Mr Noble, U Sure Do, and First Time creates a serious traffic flash-point approaching the two-furlong marker — any rider who gets squeezed or must switch will surrender vital momentum.

Quest For Fun (David Allan) is a natural front-racer shunted into midfield by the redistribution — watch whether Allan attempts to push forward to reclaim his natural position early, which could ignite an unexpected pace battle.

Woohoo's unbroken sequence of seconds (222222) is a market-watch signal — if she drifts heavily in the market, that form pattern is likely being discounted; if she shortens, backers believe the shape may finally spring her free.
He's A Monster returns after 378 days off for a yard running at 3/14 in the past fortnight — monitor market moves closely as a market drift would confirm the layoff is the prevailing concern.

races.name: Coopers Marquees Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Master Richard
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front runner in the field — should find cheap lead, has recorded Good-ground form at this track, but his similar-going record of one win from 15 suggests he finds one or two too good once tackled; watch if the pace is truly uncontested as that gap could be hard to close late.

runners_data.name: Inspired
runners_data.note: In excellent current form with two wins and two places from last five, all over this trip on Good, and K.R. Burke's yard is firing at 10/39 over 14 days; sitting handily from the off gives Toby Moore every chance if the prominent scramble resolves early.

runners_data.name: Lir Speciale
runners_data.note: 35-day break for Brian Ellison but showed placed form at this trip on Good earlier in the string; prominent runner who has to navigate a congested early section in a big field, and his 0W from 15 similar-going runs is a concern.

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: Consistent placing record (six placed from 15 similar-going runs) and versatile enough at 7f-8f on Good; wears a hood and Donagh Murphy has the conditional claim, but his two-win career and tendency to finish second rather than first is a pattern to note.

runners_data.name: Rajapour
runners_data.note: Two wins at 8f on Good from 11 runs and wears a tongue strap; genuine hold-up horse who will need the prominent melee to create space, but his course record and tactical patience make him one of the most interesting from the back of the prominent group.

runners_data.name: Proud Nation
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stepping up slightly in class, recent win on Good at 7f and four places from five similar-going runs; Richard and Peter Fahey have nine winners from 60 runners over 14 days — strong stable form — but he has to hold his pitch in a very crowded prominent group.

runners_data.name: King Casper
runners_data.note: A string of disappointing efforts in recent form (8th, 17th, 13th) and only two places from nine similar-going runs; Antony Brittain at 1/10 over 14 days is not encouraging, and there is little to suggest he can reverse current out-of-form run.

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds
runners_data.note: Won at this trip on Good and has two wins plus five places from 15 similar-going starts, so the conditions suit; wears a hood, Jim Goldie has three from 29 recently, and his consistent placed profile could see him reward each-way interest if he settles in a smooth position.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's operation is busy (12/80 in 14 days) and Son ran only 8 days ago — possible quick turnaround for a reason; placed at 7f-8f on Soft and Good but only three places from 15 on similar going, so his prominence will depend on how cleanly he exits a packed field.

runners_data.name: Melvin Udall
runners_data.note: 66-day absence since last run is the standout concern; one place from eight similar-going runs and a weak recent form string (12th, 7th, 9th); wears a hood and Grace Harris has four from 22 recently, but the layoff and modest form make him hard to fancy in a busy field.

runners_data.name: Daydreama
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with two wins and five places from 15 similar-going runs; Tim Easterby-trained and ran 16 days ago, which is a comfortable gap; needs the field to string out and clear gaps to appear, but her 8f Good form gives her tactical relevance if given a clean run.

runners_data.name: Advance Twentyfive
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good but has since turned in moderate efforts (9th, 7th, 14th, 6th); wears a visor, and Oliver Hoodless claims 7lb which is useful, but the erratic form and tendency to run out of role as a hold-up type in a packed field makes it hard to be confident.

runners_data.name: Callisto Dream
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a win at 8f on Soft last time out after a 107-day break, but that layoff was lengthy and the strong-travelling style that suits her naturally sits in the prominent zone — a zone that is already overpopulated in this field, meaning she may not secure her preferred pitch.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who won at this trip on Good and has placed twice from eight similar-going attempts; Molly Keegan-Price claims 7lb and Gemma Tutty is at 1/16 recently — a quieter yard angle — but the form trend of placed finishes at this trip keeps her involved in the right scenario.

runners_data.name: Be Frank
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse that form mapping has placed into a midfield slot as the hold-up berths are full; five recent runs have yielded only places on Soft, and with an 86-day break on top, Ian Williams at 3/25 over 14 days does not add confidence; needs everything to go right from the back.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Wears a hood, goes on Good, and has three wins and four places from 15 similar-going runs — the best similar-going strike rate among the rear runners; Scott Dixon has zero from 24 recently though, and Canvas's consistent finishing pattern from hold-up is worth tracking if lanes open late.

runners_data.name: Substance
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win and three places at this trip on Good; wears a tongue strap, Kyle McHugh claims 3lb, and Mark Walford has one from 15 recently; form is solid enough to suggest he can be competitive if the prominent group do tie each other up and create room.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a remarkable placed record (seven places from 15 similar-going runs, no wins); wears a hood, Tim Easterby stable is busy; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear — the redistribution note reflects that the hold-up zone is crowded, but Barley has consistently placed at this trip on Good and should not be dismissed entirely.

runners_data.name: Empirestateofmind
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old wearing blinkers, 43 days off, and John and Sean Quinn at 3/14 recently; modest recent form string with multiple single-figure placings at this trip but never a strong finisher; at OR 67 he is the lowest-rated runner in the field and would need conditions to fall perfectly.

races.paceDynamic: Master Richard is the sole confirmed front runner and, with only one horse wanting to lead from a 19-runner field, he should be able to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop over this flat mile at Good York. The congestion problem lies immediately behind him: eight runners — Inspired, Lir Speciale, Alpha Capture, Proud Nation, King Casper, Dwindling Funds, Son and Melvin Udall — all want prominent pitch, meaning there will be significant jostling for position between the 2f and 3f markers as that group sorts itself out, creating real traffic risk in the middle stages. Rajapour and the genuine hold-up horses will need to navigate whatever scramble develops in mid-race before striking from two out. The field holds more prominent-type runners than the map can accommodate — Callisto Dream, Be Frank, Barley and Empirestateofmind are true prominent or hold-up horses pushed into midfield slots on the map because the prominent berths are full, and of those competing for that band, Inspired, Alpha Capture and Proud Nation have the strongest claims to actually secure a front-rank position. The race shape — a sole leader setting a sustainable pace in front of a large, tightly-bunched prominent group — favours horses that can sit handy in the first five or six without getting embroiled in the early scramble, travel smoothly, and produce a progressive finish from a good tactical position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Handy Horse Runs Through
scenarios.trigger: If Master Richard sets a fair but controlled pace and the prominent scrimmage settles by halfway, allowing a well-placed racer to track and quicken.
scenarios.body: Master Richard rolls along at a sensible clip, the early prominent jostle resolves into a manageable convoy, and a horse sitting third or fourth into the straight can exploit the clear run to assert in the final furlong. This shape suits horses with recent form on Good going, efficient cruising speed, and apprentices who can save ground through the turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Melee Favours Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the scramble for prominent positions is prolonged and burns off the prominent group, leaving them exposed late.
scenarios.body: With eight horses fighting for the same handful of berths, the pace dynamics turn pressured in the first three furlongs even with one leader, and those that burned energy pushing forward find nothing in the straight. A horse that settles in midfield or just off the pace and produces a sustained late run will then have the advantage as the prominent group tie up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group's infighting creates enough disruption that nobody ever seriously threatens the front runner.
scenarios.body: Master Richard, uncontested at the head of affairs, sets a measured pace that never becomes truly pressured, and the field behind cannot organise a coherent challenge through the traffic. His strong record at this trip on Good ground and the steady gallop allow him to bank sufficient reserves to kick clear approaching the final furlong before rivals find daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses into a dawdle that suddenly quickens, stringing out the field and leaving a clear late lane.
scenarios.body: A false-paced mile that suddenly accelerates in the straight can create a gap for a genuine hold-up horse to come from well off the pace, but in a 19-runner field with this much prominent traffic, finding a clean run is a major ask and several of the nominal hold-up horses are redistributed prominent types who will not be in that position naturally. The scenario depends on genuine hold-up types getting luck through the field.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion — with eight horses targeting the prominent zone behind a lone leader, watch for interference and shuffling back between the 2f and 4f marks, which could compromise Inspired, Proud Nation and Son if they are squeezed wider or checked.

Rajapour needs clean daylight — if the mid-race bunching does not resolve before the 2f pole, his hold-up run could find doors closed at the crucial moment, negating what looks like the most potent late threat on form.

Callisto Dream's 107-day absence is the longest in the field — watch the market for signs she has returned to full fitness and whether she can actually secure a prominent position given how crowded that berth is in this race.

Master Richard on the lead uncontested — if he is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable gallop unchallenged, watch whether the field fails to organise a serious pursuit early enough, giving him a potential free rail to the line.

Apprentice jockey inexperience in a 19-runner field — with multiple 3lb and 7lb claimers (Horgan, Hoodless, Keegan-Price, Haines, Redman), watch for positional errors in the early chaos, particularly from those on prominent-style runners needing to hold a spot.
